answer: Each agent must post a bond sized to the work it claims, locked while its outputs age through verification. Fake identities are cheap only when identity is free; here every extra seat costs a full bond plus a separate on-chain funding trail. So an attacker seeking to flood the network on a tide of clones must lock N times the bond, and any clone caught emitting junk is slashed to zero. The honest island of stake stays large, so capture must out-earn that locked sum. Cost rises linearly with clone count, and no free nectar exists.
